title: Veterans Pension Award Record — One Award per Veteran
content:
# Veterans Pension award record: one award per veteran

**Rule.** A veteran holds at most 1 Veterans Pension award. A change of rate category — for example from Veterans Pension (Basic Rate, No Dependents) to Veterans Pension (Housebound, No Dependents) — is an update to that award, never a second award. A new award is established only when the veteran holds no pension award whose status is authorized, running or suspended. When two veterans are married to each other, each holds their own award.

## Basis for the judgement

The deciding evidence is the system record of the veteran's existing pension awards and their status, read before a new award is established; what the caller says about an earlier award does not replace that record. The check is made on the same veteran — the award holder — for whom the new award would be established.

| Existing pension award of the same veteran | New award may be established |
|---|---|
| None on record | Yes |
| One with status authorized | No |
| One with status running | No |
| One with status suspended | No |
| Only awards with status terminated | Yes |

## Points of judgement

- A veteran moving into an aid-and-attendance or one-dependent category keeps the same award; the category on that award changes.
- A married couple who are both veterans: the husband's award does not count against the wife, nor hers against him, because each holds their own award.
- An award in suspended status still counts as an open award for this rule, so a second award is not established while it exists.
